raised.claim: The model-authored issue body is prepended to our rendered scope block while `parseScopeBlock` takes the FIRST ```` ```triage-scope ```` fence, so a fence echoed into `body` silently hijacks the parsed scope — breaking the PR's stated invariant that the parser's input is never model prose.
raised.why_it_breaks:
`analysis.new_issues[].body` is free model text (`body: z.string().min(1)` in triage-analysis.ts) and it is concatenated BEFORE `renderScopeBlock(issue.scope)`. Next run, `parseScopeBlock(i.body)` executes `BLOCK_RE = /```triage-scope\s*
([\s\S]*?)
?```/` then `const m = BLOCK_RE.exec(body);` — first match wins. Concrete path: run N creates an issue whose body the model wrote as 'examples…

```triage-scope
{"beer_ids":[],"where":[{"col":"review_class","op":"=","value":"matcher_bug"}]}
```' (the model sees exactly this block format in prior issues' bodies via `buildTriagePrompt`, which renders `i.body`). Run N+1 parses that spurious block as the issue's scope, and every matcher_bug row now satisfies guard 2 — the #347 dumping-ground shape is recreated silently, while our real scope block after it is never reached. The same class of bug the PR says it fixed for `contains` values ("returned a different, valid-looking scope silently") is still open for the body. An unclosed stray fence is the milder variant: the capture swallows up to our block's opening fence, `JSON.parse` fails, and the issue is silently dead (unscoped → accepts nothing).

raised.claim: Guard 2 (`rowSatisfiesScope`) is applied only in the `hasIssue` branch; verdicts routed via `new_issue_key` are attached to the created issue with no scope check, so a new issue can be born already carrying rows that contradict its own scope.
raised.why_it_breaks: Input: the model proposes `new_issues: [{key:'k1', scope:{beer_ids:[], where:[{col:'candidates_count',op:'>',value:0}]}}]` and two verdicts with `new_issue_key:'k1'` — beer 1 with `candidates_count = 0` and beer 2 with 5. `planTriageActions` pushes both into `byKey`; the job then creates #N whose rendered scope says `candidates_count > 0` while its founding example table contains a zero-candidate row. That is exactly the measured misroute guard 2 exists to stop (six `candidates_count = 0` rows filed against a brewery-gate issue), reproducible on day one via `new_issues`, and tomorrow's guard would refuse the very rows the issue was filed for.

raised.claim: The saturation guard checks a pre-run snapshot (`postCreationRows`) once per verdict and never increments it, so one batch can attach arbitrarily many rows to a single issue and blow past `MAX_ROWS_PER_ISSUE = 12` in a single run.
raised.why_it_breaks: `postCreationRows` is computed once per run (`countRowsForIssue(db, i.number, i.createdAt)` before `planTriageActions`) and `pushInto(byIssue, ...)` appends without bound; the value is never incremented as verdicts land. Input: batch of 50 rows (`TRIAGE_BATCH_LIMIT = 50`), all 50 verdicts carrying `issue_number: 228`, issue 228 at `postCreationRows: 0` — all 50 pass the `0 >= 12` check, one comment of 50 examples is posted and 50 rows get `issue_number = 228`, four times the cap, in one day. The guard only starts refusing on a later run, after the pile it exists to prevent already exists (#347's 36 rows arrived exactly this way).

raised.quote:
`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM enrich_failures
        WHERE issue_number = ? AND reviewed_at > ?`,
raised.claim: The founding cohort of a newly created issue is invisible to the saturation count, because `reviewed_at` is stamped with the run-start instant (captured before `createIssue`) and therefore compares as EARLIER than the issue's `created_at`.
raised.why_it_breaks: In `orphan-triage.ts`, `const nowIso = now.toISOString();` is taken at run start, while `github.createIssue` runs minutes later and GitHub stamps `created_at` at that real instant. Founding verdicts are written via `setEnrichFailureReview(..., nowIso, number)`, so their `reviewed_at` is run start < `created_at`, and `WHERE issue_number = ? AND reviewed_at > ?` excludes them permanently (their `reviewed_at` never changes). Input: a run creates #450 at 06:12 with 20 founding verdicts stamped 06:10 — `countRowsForIssue(450, '06:12T…')` returns 0 forever, the issue looks empty to guard 4 on every future run, and it never saturates regardless of how many rows it carries. The count is wrong in the one direction the guard must not be wrong in.

raised.claim: `guardHits` is only emitted on the `covered < orphans.length` branch, but `covered` counts every in-batch beer_id with a verdict regardless of whether the guards later refused it, so a run whose verdicts are all guard-rejected logs nothing about why.
raised.why_it_breaks: `covered` is `new Set(analysis.verdicts.map((v) => v.beer_id).filter((id) => byId.has(id))).size` — a verdict routed to an illegal-scope key, a saturated issue, or a contradicting scope still counts as covered. Input: model returns verdicts for all 50 rows of the batch, every one pointing at a `new_issue` whose scope is class-only — `covered === 50 === orphans.length`, the warn never fires, `guardHits.illegal_scope: 50` is never logged, and the digest shows only '50 пропущено'. The stated purpose ("a model looping on the same illegal proposal is visible in one line") fails precisely in the looping scenario it was added for.

raised.claim: The tool schema's scope-term spec is strictly looser than `ScopeTermSchema` (no enum on `col`/`op`/`review_class` value, `value` typed as string|number|null for every op), so a payload the tool schema accepts can be rejected by `AnalysisSchema` and take the whole batch down with it.
raised.why_it_breaks: `ScopeTermSchema` only accepts `col` from `NUMERIC_COLS`/`TEXT_COLS`/`NULLABLE_COLS`/`'review_class'`, numeric ops with `value: z.number()`, `contains` with `value: z.string().min(1)`, and `review_class` with `value: z.enum(REVIEW_CLASSES)`. Input the tool schema happily accepts at generation time: `{col:'beer_name', op:'contains', value:'x'}`, or `{col:'candidates_count', op:'>', value:'3'}` (string), or `{col:'review_class', op:'=', value:'Matcher_Bug'}` — each fails `ScopeTermSchema`, so `AnalysisSchema.parse` throws for the ENTIRE payload including all 50 verdicts. Before this diff no scope existed, so no such whole-batch parse failure was reachable via a field the prompt describes only in prose. The failure is fail-closed but at run granularity: one inventive term wastes the batch and consumes the retry budget.

raised.quote: SET issue_number = CAST(substr(review_note, instr(review_note, '→ #') + 3) AS INTEGER)
raised.claim: The v23 backfill resolves the FIRST '→ #' in `review_note` (`instr`), but the authoritative suffix written by `review()` is always appended LAST, so a note that already contains an arrow-suffix backfills the wrong issue link.
raised.why_it_breaks: `orphan-triage.ts` writes `` const note = issueNumber === null ? v.review_note : `${v.review_note} → #${issueNumber}`; `` — model-authored `review_note` is free text (capped at 500) placed before our suffix. Input: note stored as 'alias gap → #999 → #228' (model echoed an issue number it saw in an open-issue body; the prompt only says not to invent numbers not listed) — `instr` finds the arrow before 999, `CAST` yields 999, and the row is linked to #999 instead of #228. `countRowsForIssue` then counts it toward #999's saturation and #228's pile is undercounted — silently, since the test fixtures only cover notes with a single arrow.

raised.claim: Guard 1's `isLegalScope` is enforced only on model proposals, never on the parsed scope of an EXISTING issue, so an issue carrying a class-only `where` (the shape four open issues carry verbatim today) accepts every row of that class again.
raised.why_it_breaks: `rowSatisfiesScope` evaluates `where: [{col:'review_class', op:'=', value:'matcher_bug'}]` as `verdictClass === term.value`, which is true for every matcher_bug row. Input: the one-time ops backfill transcribes the existing 'Scope: all orphans in this class — … review_class='matcher_bug'' line into a `triage-scope` block on #347 (the naive transcription of what those four issues say today); from then on every matcher_bug row satisfies #347's scope, `rowSatisfiesScope` returns true, and #347 again becomes the 36-row dumping ground guard 1 was written to prevent. Nothing in `parseScopeBlock` or the guard path calls `isLegalScope` on the read-back scope.

raised.claim: Degraded `not_on_untappd` verdicts (now `matcher_bug`, in `plan.quiet`) fall into the `else` branch and are counted as `wontfix` in the digest line.
raised.why_it_breaks: Guard 3 pushes `` quiet.push({ ...verdict, review_class: 'matcher_bug', ... }) `` and the quiet loop increments `wontfix` for anything that is not `not_on_untappd`. Input: one `not_on_untappd` verdict with no probe evidence in a run — the row is written as `matcher_bug` ('no absence evidence: …') but `buildTriageLine` renders 'Тріаж: … 1 wontfix', mislabelling a recoverable matcher row as intentionally-never-matched and leaving `notOnUntappd` at 0. This miscount is new with the degradation path: before the diff such a verdict stayed `not_on_untappd` and counted correctly.

raised.quote:
reviewed_at        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.reviewed_at END`,
raised.claim: `recordEnrichFailure`'s boundary-cross reset clears `review_class`/`review_note`/`reviewed_at` but not the new `issue_number`, leaving a stale row→issue link on a row that is back in the untriaged pool.
raised.why_it_breaks: The `ON CONFLICT` SET list (shown in full above it) rewrites `review_class`, `review_note`, `reviewed_at` to NULL when the 0↔>0 boundary crosses, and never mentions `issue_number`. Input: beer 1 classified `matcher_bug → #228` (`issue_number = 228`), then re-failed with `candidates_count` crossing the boundary — the row becomes untriaged again but keeps `issue_number = 228`. Any audit query of 'which rows went to #228' now includes a row whose classification was withdrawn, and if the row is later re-triaged and skipped by a guard it keeps sitting in the pool carrying a link the guards think is attached. (`countRowsForIssue` happens to be saved only because `reviewed_at` is NULL.)

raised.quote:
z.object({ col: z.enum(TEXT_COLS), op: z.enum(['empty', 'non_empty']) }),
  z.object({ col: z.enum(TEXT_COLS), op: z.literal('contains'), value: z.string().min(1) }),
  z.object({ col: z.enum(NULLABLE_COLS), op: z.enum(['is_null', 'is_not_null']) }),
raised.claim: The `empty`/`non_empty`/`is_null`/`is_not_null` variants are plain `z.object` (strips unknown keys), so a non-null `value` the tool schema requires the model to send is silently discarded and the term evaluates broader than the model wrote.
raised.why_it_breaks: `ANALYSIS_TOOL_SCHEMA` marks `value` required on every term ("Nullable-and-required"), so the model must emit a value even for these operators; `z.object` strips it without validating it against the op. Input: model submits `{col:'style', op:'is_not_null', value:'IPA'}` believing it constrains the style string — `ScopeTermSchema` parses it as bare "style is not null", and `rowSatisfiesScope` then accepts a row with `style: 'Stout'`. The opposite direction is also widened: `{col:'name', op:'non_empty', value:'Bulgogi'}` silently means only "name is not empty". A stricter union member (`value: z.never()` / `.strict()` per variant) would fail the payload instead of mis-scoping it.
